scenes.text: You are standing in a beautiful, fifty-mile strip of Yellowstone National Park, but you are actually in the only place on Earth where a legal loophole theoretically allows you to get away with a perfect crime.
Dubbed the Zone of Death, this specific Idaho section of the park is completely immune to prosecution because of a bizarre overlap in the United States Constitution.

The law guarantees your right to a jury from the state and district where the crime occurred, but since this district belongs to Wyoming while the land is in Idaho, and zero people live here, a jury cannot physically be formed.
Though scholars have begged Congress to fix this terrifying legal loophole for decades, it remains open, so would you ever dare to camp in this zone? Comment below and follow for more.

meta.title: The 50-Mile Strip Where Crimes Are Technically Legal #shorts
